title: The 1924-25 Brownlee records and 'Peculiar Rag'
summary: Harry dates his first records to 1924-25 with Brownlee, tells of sharing composer credit on 'Peculiar' and 'Dirty Rag', and Russell reports on Brownlee in Pensacola.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And by the way, when were the first records that you ever made? Can you remember? That was with Brown Lee's band.
I think it was 1924 and 25. Yeah, we have...
An all okay record. Yeah, we have that record up at Tulane now. I wish I had it here to play for you and get your reaction. I don't have a copy here.
Those were your compositions, weren't there, Harry? One of them was.
Yeah, those are the shields on there. When I first found the record, I thought it was your brother. Of course, that was 20 years ago and I knew more about your brother then than you.

See, Brown Lee, he was... That was his introduction to Peculiar Rank. Norman Brown Lee? Yeah. And of course, the other side was Sharky's tune. Let's see, what was the name of that? Dirty Rank. Oh, yeah. Yeah. So we decided that we'd use three names on both sides. But the verse and the chorus of Peculiar was really mine. And then later Sharky recorded it again, I think with Sidney Airdman and Mel Kaisel. So he told me about this. Well, go ahead. You can make a recording. Go ahead.

By the way, Dick Allen, who works with us up at Tulane, was over in Pensacola just two weeks ago and interviewed Norman Brown. Norman, did he? Said he's getting along fine. He's president of the union over there. I understand that.
And I think he's president of the Kiwanis Club or some other club. Oh, he is? In the community, too. He seems to be a prominent fellow in the community over there, too.
We played lots of jobs together. He's a great fellow.
